name: workqueues
title: Work queues
summary: The Operations Center's shared to-do system: queue definitions with an owner role, a named lead, a backup and an escalation route, and work items raised from other modules' events (overdue dispatch, low stock, waiting approvals, cases past target, failed payouts, mismatches) with deadlines, assignment and automatic escalation. Also the My work queues view, the dashboard's needs-attention tiles, the day-end review, the daily routine and saved filters.
owns: Queue definitions: area, owner role, lead, backup, escalation route, default deadline, which events open and close items, the screen where the work is done
Intake rules mapping source events to work items, with de-duplication and automatic resolution when the source is fixed
Work items: subject, deadline, priority, state, assignee, escalation level, notes and history
Deadline and escalation engine (due soon, overdue, escalate to the next step, backup cover when the lead is away)
My work queues view and the admin dashboard needs-attention summary with the team on shift
Daily operating routine checks and the day-end review (unresolved commitments, failed payouts, upcoming campaigns, next-day shipping)
Seller-visible tasks for items that concern a seller (e.g. overdue dispatch, scenario 5)
notOwns: The work itself: items link to the owning module's screen and endpoints (orders, shipping, finance, catalog, sellers, support, trust...)
Staff roles, backups as a staffing fact and approval requests: access (workqueues reads role members and backups)
Export files: reports (workqueues registers a dataset)

stateMachines.name: Work item
stateMachines.notes: Deadline state (on_time, due_soon, overdue) and escalation level are separate from the state: the sweep job moves them, publishes workqueues.item.overdue once per item and escalates along the queue's route. Reassigning keeps the state (an item in progress or waiting stays so with the new assignee). Waiting keeps the deadline unless the queue has pauseWhileWaiting: then the sweep ignores waiting items and resume moves dueAt later by the time since waiting_since. Most items resolve automatically from their source's resolvesOn events (resolution outcome fixed_at_source); manual resolve needs a note; dismiss needs a reason. A raise with the same dedupeKey reopens a dismissed item only if the source fires again after dismissal.

stateMachines.name: Day-end review
stateMachines.notes: Built daily before dayEndReviewTime. Complete requires every item checked (a note is required for items with open overdue work) and sends the summary to the shared roles. Missed at midnight market time if not completed; the next day's review lists it.

stateMachines.name: Routine check
stateMachines.notes: Generated each morning from routine templates for the owner roles on shift.

settings.desc: When an item turns due soon
Day-end review due time, market time
Who sees and receives the day-end review
Resolved items stay in the default lists this long, then are archived (kept in Postgres)
Queues created at install with placeholder leads that must be set before launch (a migration adds the fulfillment.* queues to existing installs)

LEAD_EQUALS_BACKUP.meaning: A queue's backup must be a different person from its lead

ASSIGNEE_NOT_ELIGIBLE.meaning: The assignee does not hold the queue's owner role and is not its lead or backup

ESCALATION_ROUTE_END.meaning: The item is already at the last step of the escalation route

NOTE_REQUIRED.meaning: This day-end item has overdue work; add a note explaining the plan

DAY_END_INCOMPLETE.meaning: Some day-end items are not checked yet; details.items

notes: Queues per kind (seedQueues): payment_check and payment_mismatch → finance.payment_checks; chargeback → finance.chargebacks; payout_failed → finance.payout_failures; hold_review → finance.daily_checks; launch_review and storefront_review → sellers.launch_reviews; restriction_evidence and restriction_review → sellers.restrictions; appeal_due → sellers.appeals; seller_performance → sellers.performance; low_stock → inventory.low_stock; inventory's merge candidates (manual_task with dedupeKey inventory.merge_candidate:<stockItemId>:<twinId>, raised after a catalog merge leaves two company SKUs on the same variant and condition) → inventory.merge_candidates (owner role inventory_manager, screen ops/inventory filter merge_candidates; raise() routes them there by that dedupe prefix whatever queue the caller names, while the queue is installed and active; closed by hand once merged, or by inventory with resolveBySource); unexpected_return_parcel and return_parcel_overdue (raised by warehouse) → warehouse.return_parcels; seller_owner_missing (raised by sellers) → sellers.accounts (owner role seller_manager); review_moderation_overdue (raised by reviews' moderation-sla job) → reviews.moderation (owner role trust_and_risk_manager, which holds reviews.moderation.*); official_store_reply (raised and resolved by messaging while staff owe an Official Store reply) → official_store.messages (owner role official_store_manager, not seller-visible); enforcement_reversal (raised by trust when an enforcement is reversed) → the owning team's queue, like trust_recommendation. Fulfilled by Marketly (raised and resolved by fulfillment-service with raise() and resolveBySource): fulfillment.receiving (owner role warehouse_manager, screen ops/receiving; kind receiving, dedupe fs_inbound_overdue:<inboundId> and fs_discrepancy:<inboundId>), fulfillment.reconciliation (inventory_manager, ops/inventory; manual_task, fs_stock_difference:<skuEnrollmentId>), fulfillment.requests (warehouse_manager, ops/pick-pack; pick_pack, fs_request_short:<requestId>), fulfillment.enrollments (seller_manager, admin/sellers; application_waiting, fs_enrollment:<id> and fs_sku:<id>); none is seller-visible.

How kinds close: event-raised kinds close on the events listed under consumes (chargeback on payments.chargeback.decided, payment_mismatch on finance.reconciliation.item_closed, restriction_evidence on sellers.restriction.lifted or updated, return_parcel_overdue on warehouse.return_parcel.received). seller_performance and unexpected_return_parcel are closed by hand (resolve with a note). Kinds raised through raise() (receiving, pick_pack, return_inspection, hold_review, restriction_review, seller_owner_missing, enforcement_reversal) are closed by the raising module with resolveBySource (seller_owner_missing when the seller has an active owner again; enforcement_reversal when the owning team confirmed the undo), or by hand. review_moderation_overdue closes on reviews.moderation.decided.

Deadlines from the source: product_review uses catalog.product.submitted reviewDueAt and application_waiting uses sellers.application.submitted decisionTargetAt; raise() callers pass dueAt; otherwise the queue default applies (business hours when businessHoursOnly, through settings.businessCalendar).
Archive stays in Postgres: there is no cold-storage store; archived_at only hides old resolved items from working lists. Partitioning or moving them out is a later infrastructure step.

Work queues never do the work: each item links to the owning module's screen and API. Most items close themselves when the source event arrives (resolvesOn), so a queue reflects reality without double entry.

Every queue has a named lead, a different backup and an escalation route (plan ch. 2). Install creates seedQueues with placeholders; launch readiness requires real people. Who receives an item right now comes from access.resolveRecipients(ownerRole) (lead, or the first available backup while the lead is away); queue lead and backup default to the role's lead and backup and can be set per queue.

Events consumed here use the canonical names; finance's daily reconciliation also calls raise() directly for checks that have no event. Modules without a matching event (e.g. warehouse pick-pack, purchasing receiving) call raise() and resolveBySource().

Seller-visible items (overdue dispatch, missing tracking, reply overdue) satisfy scenario 5: the Shipping Manager sees the item in ops/queues and the seller sees the same task in Seller Center (GET /api/seller/workqueues/tasks); staff notes and escalation details never reach the seller.

Saved filters can target another module's list screen (target=screen) so one place stores every manager's filters, as the ops/queues screen shows ('Overdue over 24 h, marketplace sellers' opens ops/dispatch with its filter).
Exports go through reports so that the same permission and audit rules apply to every export.
